q.t: What is a bar?
q.e: Beats are grouped into bars (measures), marked by bar lines.

q.t: In a time signature, the top number tells you…
o: how many beats in each bar
how many bars in the song

q.t: In a time signature, a bottom number of 4 means…
o: a quarter note gets one beat

q.t: How many beats are in each bar of 4/4?
How many beats are in each bar of 3/4?
Which time signature is a waltz?
q.e: A waltz sways in threes: ONE two three.

q.t: What does BPM stand for?
q.e: BPM = beats per minute, the speed on the metronome.

q.t: At 60 BPM, how long does each beat last?
What is the big C sometimes written instead of 4/4?
q.e: C stands for common time, another name for 4/4.

q.t: Which beat of a bar usually feels strongest?
q.e: Beat 1 is the landmark — 'ONE two three four'.

q.t: Which is faster?
At 120 BPM, how long is each beat?
At 30 BPM, how long is each beat?
In 3/4, which single note fills a whole bar?
q.e: Dotted half = 3 beats, exactly one 3/4 bar.

q.t: Why can't a whole note fit in a 3/4 bar?
o: It lasts 4 beats; the bar holds 3
q.e: 4 beats is more than the 3 the bar holds.

q.t: Which song is in 3/4?
q.e: Happy Birthday sways in threes. The others are in 4/4.

q.t: What does Andante mean?
What does Presto mean?
In Indian music, the first, strongest beat of a taal is called…
q.e: Sam is the landmark beat, like beat 1 of a bar.

q.t: Why do musicians group beats into bars?
o: So you always know where 'one' is
Only to make music look neat
q.e: Bars give landmarks: 'start at bar 9' and a strong beat 1 to stay in place.

q.t: How many beats does Keherwa taal have?
How many beats does Teentaal have?
Dadra taal (6 beats, 3 + 3) is most like…
q.e: 6/8 is also 6 beats felt as two groups of 3.

q.t: A song is 4/4 at 60 BPM. How long is one bar?
A song is 3/4 at 120 BPM. How long is one bar?
q.e: Each beat = ½ second; 3 × ½ = 1½ seconds.

q.t: Which bar is complete in 4/4?
Which bar is complete in 3/4?
6/8 has 6 eighth-note beats. How is it usually felt?
q.e: ONE two three FOUR five six — two rolling groups of three.

q.t: What is the difference between 4/4 and 80 BPM?
o: 4/4 groups the beats; 80 BPM sets the speed
4/4 is the speed; 80 BPM is the grouping
q.e: Time signature = how beats are grouped. Tempo = how fast they go.

q.t: Why can most Keherwa film songs be strummed in 4/4?
q.e: 8 beats in groups of 4 is the same as two bars of 4/4.

q.t: A 4/4 song has 32 bars. How many beats is that?
That 32-bar 4/4 song is played at 64 BPM. How long is it?
At 90 BPM, how long is one beat?
One beat lasts ¾ of a second. What is the BPM?
In 2/4, how many eighth notes fill one bar?
In 3/4, a bar has a half note. What fills the rest of the bar?
q.e: 3 − 2 = 1 beat left, which is one quarter note.

q.t: How many full cycles of Keherwa fit into one Teentaal cycle?
In 6/8, what note gets one beat?
Why does a bottom number of 4 mean a quarter note?
o: A quarter note is ¼ of a whole note
q.e: It is a fraction: 4/4 = four quarters per bar; 3/4 = three quarters.

q.t: You speed up from 60 BPM to 120 BPM. What happens to each beat?
q.e: Twice as many beats share the same minute, so each lasts half as long: 1 s → ½ s.
